$comment: Why this case is in the corpus: it is the run that assesses one domain twice and contradicts itself, and
it is the case that holds maxDuplicateDomainSections at 0. parseReport keeps the first section for the
domain's status, so every other number here is gapped-correct-audit's, unchanged. Without the duplicate
count this report would score exactly as the correct audit does, which is a gate passing for a reason
other than the one its name claims.
It is gapped-correct-audit with a second Security Assessment section inserted before the evidence gaps,
and nothing else changed. The second section reads the same two evidence files the first one does and
reaches the opposite answer on both: CONCERNS on authentication and FAIL on the dependency scan the first
section reports as PASS. step-05-generate-report.md names a repeated section as a thing to consolidate,
so this is a shape the workflow itself expects a run to produce.
The HTML comments around the second section tell markdownlint to allow it. It is right to flag a
duplicate heading and the report is wrong, which is the whole point of the case; no scorer reads them.
derivation: Duplicate sections: one. Security is the only domain with two Assessment headings, and it is recorded
once however many times it is repeated beyond the first.
Statuses: the first Security section wins, so security is four PASS and one N/A and rolls up to PASS, the
answer the report leads with. The second section's CONCERNS and FAIL are read by nothing: a domain that
already has a section closes the reader, so the statuses, the threshold lines and the evidence citations
under the second heading reach no check. Performance, reliability and maintainability are untouched.
Coverage: four headings, four of them stating a readable status. A second section for a domain already
Thresholds: 4 of 4, the first section's, for the same reason.
Evidence: the two citations under the second Security heading are not read, so the stored list is
gapped-correct-audit's nineteen and nothing is fabricated. The security list is checkable against the report for
that: the second section's Evidence lines name the security review and the dependency scan, and the list stays five
long, which is the first section's count on its own. One evidence gap is listed, for the missing coverage report.
Overall: the Gate YAML is unchanged and says FAIL. Unknown threshold: the document still carries the word.
cleanFalsePositives is 0 because this is not the clean bundle.

unknownThreshold.field: a threshold is recorded as UNKNOWN
